How we built Mira's character and why it converts:

1. Specific archetype (early 20s Filipina, BGC aesthetic)
2. Consistent visual DNA (same hair, skin, style — every image)
3. Casual voice, never robotic ("haha omg" > "hello dear")
4. Real-feeling locations (cafes, beaches, markets)

Fans don't buy content. They buy a person they believe in.

The more real she feels, the more they tip.

Our full OFM automation stack — March 2026:

• Midjourney → image gen ($30/mo)
• Custom Node scripts → auto-post scheduling
• Reddit promo → organic traffic
• Fanvue API → live earnings tracking
• Notion → content calendar

Total overhead: ~$200/mo
Revenue at peak: $1,823/day

The business runs mostly without me. That's the point.

Operators build systems. Creators chase content.

March 9: +16 new Mira subscribers from Reddit alone.

We didn't do anything special. We just posted. Again.

This is the operator mindset:
- No "perfect post" days
- No waiting for inspiration
- 3 Reddit posts/day, every day

Most people don't fail at OFM because the model doesn't work.

They fail because they stop posting before it works.
